text:
maria: seeing a p99 jump in shared-gpu pool 'pool-a' starting ~12:22 UTC, from ~65ms -> 420ms. Not a full outage but sustained tail. Anyone else? :eyes:
kevin: which models/routes affected? any recent rollouts?
maria: mostly gpt-medium-ish variants (open-*) and a single tenant looks suspicious: tenant_alpha sending a ton of short requests. No infra deploys in that window.
raj: could be batching artifact + kv cache thrash. Short, high-QPS requests can break batching and evict prefix KV entries. Do we have cache hit stats?
maria: quick snapshot from profiler (12:21-12:25):
```
batch_stats: avg_batch_size=1.9 p50=2 p90=5 p99=9
kernel_selector: flip_count=12 (small_batch_kernel <-> large_batch_kernel)
kv_cache_hit_rate=0.36 -> down from 0.78
cpu->gpu memcpy wait spikes at p95
```
maria: also saw several kernel switches coinciding with the spike timestamps.
elaine: hmm kernel autoselect thrashes when the sequence length distribution is bimodal. Small batches pick one optimized kernel, then larger ones force another -> context switch overhead. Combined with KV misses that's nasty.
kevin: do we have per-tenant concurrency / lease limits on pool-a? if tenant_alpha is hammering many tiny requests it might monopolize batch slots.
maria: pool config: soft_leases enabled, per-tenant_concurrency cap = 50 (global), tenant_alpha peaked at ~48 concurrent, so near cap but not exceeding. However their request pattern is very bursty (many short 1-2 token inferences).
raj: small requests produce tiny batches -> lower throughput -> the scheduler tries to fill but gives up quickly -> increases kernel switches. Also KV entries for warm prefixes get evicted because small seqs don't reuse longer prefixes. Result: cache miss -> full compute every time.
elaine: short-term mitigation: 1) apply token-bucket throttle for tenant_alpha 2) increase kv_cache_reservation for warm sessions 3) bump batch wait for small requests to 6ms on pool-a. Thoughts?
kevin: +1 to kv_reservation. Throttling is easiest to push fast. Also consider grouping by estimated seq_len in the batching queue before assembling a batch. That will reduce kernel flips.
maria: I can push throttling rule now: set QPS cap to 35 for tenant_alpha on pool-a. Also creating a KV pin policy for sessions from that tenant with heat > 0.7.
perf-bot: deploy-bot: canary config change "throttle/tenant_alpha/qps=35" applied to pool-a at 12:40 UTC (canary 5%). Link: https://deploys/release/5678
kevin: after throttle, monitor p99 and kv_hit_rate for 30m. If improves, roll to 100%.
raj: medium-term: change batching heuristic: prefer grouping by estimated input length + model-variant; and avoid kernel flips by adding sticky kernel hint for a short window after a switch. Might need runtime change to kernel_selector.
elaine: owners: maria -> immediate throttle & KV pin; kevin -> change batching queue prototype; raj -> instrument kernel switch tracer and KV eviction correlation; I'll own rollout coordination.
maria: initial telemetry after throttle (12:45 snapshot): p99 dropped from 420ms -> 85ms, kv_hit_rate increased 0.36 -> 0.65, avg_batch_size stable at 2.4. Early win. :tada:
kevin: nice. Let's not celebrate too early but good sign. Add an alert: if kernel_switch_rate > 5/min and kv_hit_rate < 0.5 fire a perf-regression pager.
maria: filing a short postmortem draft and perf investigation doc, will link here.
elaine: also add a follow-up RFC for hard per-tenant soft-lease enforcement and per-session KV reservations. This is recurring.
perf-bot: incident-bot: ticket created ENG-PLAT-1452 "soft-lease imbalance -> kernel thrash & kv miss on pool-a" assigned to maria, kevin, raj.
maria: thanks all. monitoring continues. :+1:
